transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. It's nice to meet you too. 

Um, I'm here because I keep having these nights where I eat an amount of food that honestly scares me. Like, I’ll start with some leftovers after I finish grading papers, and then I just... I keep going. I’ll end up going through cereal, crackers, peanut butter, and even whatever snacks I packed for my classroom. It's just becoming a really big problem.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit to try to undo them?
No, I don't do that. I've never made myself throw up.
During these episodes, do you feel unable to stop eating or control how much you’re eating?

Yes, that's exactly it. Once I start, it feels like the reasonable, teacher part of me is just watching from the outside. I'll be in my head telling myself, Joan, stop, but... my hands just keep opening things. I just keep putting food in my mouth until I’m painfully full. I really have no control over it once it begins.
After these eating episodes, do you do anything to try to make up for the eating, like taking laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

Yes, I do. Um... after one of those bad nights, I’ll tell myself I’m not allowed to eat breakfast or lunch at school the next day. And I exercise a lot to try and make up for it. I’ll stay out on the trail for hours, or I'll force myself to do extra yoga... even when my body is shaky and I'm just completely exhausted.
About how often do these binge-and-make-up cycles happen?

For the past few months... well, there has rarely been a week without at least one night where I eat far more than I meant to. And then the next day, I try to make up for it by not eating at school, or pushing myself through a really long walk or extra yoga. So it's happening at least once a week, sometimes more.
How much does your body shape or weight affect how you feel about yourself as a person?

It affects me a lot. Um... if I look even a little softer around my stomach, or if my pants feel tight before a staff meeting, I honestly feel like I've failed at everything. It really doesn't matter how well my students are doing or how prepared I am for the day. My weight and shape just completely take over how I feel about myself as a person.
